# People and Talent Stage Contracts

One entry per desk in the People Talent Command Desk suite. Use these when running the suite as a continuous program of work, so a desk can carry work into the next stage instead of telling the user to invoke another skill.

## Stage order

```text
workforce-planning-desk
  -> job-architecture-leveling-desk
  -> sourcing-pipeline-desk
  -> structured-interview-design-desk
  -> candidate-evaluation-debrief-desk
  -> offer-compensation-desk
  -> onboarding-desk
  -> people-operations-records-desk
  -> performance-review-calibration-desk
  -> career-framework-progression-desk
  -> talent-review-succession-desk
  -> manager-enablement-desk
  -> engagement-retention-desk
  -> compensation-review-cycle-desk
  -> policy-handbook-desk
  -> employee-relations-desk
  -> leave-accommodation-desk
  -> offboarding-separation-desk
  -> people-analytics-desk
```

The order is a dependency chain, not a mandatory itinerary. The first two stages make a role real: the headcount that funds it and the definition that levels it. The next four are the hire, from channel to signed offer. The next two are the join: the first ninety days, and the record that turns an accepted offer into an employee. The next six are the employment cycle, where people are assessed, progressed, succeeded, managed, engaged, and paid. The next three are the obligation layer that the cycle keeps colliding with: the policy, the case, and the leave. Then the exit. Then the measurement that decides which of the eighteen stages above gets changed next year.

Most requests run a subsequence and enter partway: an approved opening enters at `job-architecture-leveling-desk`, a stalled pipeline enters at `sourcing-pipeline-desk`, a manager arguing that a candidate is a level higher enters at `job-architecture-leveling-desk` rather than at the offer, a resignation enters at `offboarding-separation-desk` and pushes backward into engagement and compensation, a complaint enters at `employee-relations-desk` on a retaliation clock that started at the protected activity rather than at the report, and a leadership question about attrition enters at `people-analytics-desk` and pushes backward until it lands on a manager, a band, or a level. Never run a stage ahead of the packet state it consumes, and never skip a stage the source facts show is load-bearing.

Three dependencies are structural rather than conventional. Nothing downstream of `job-architecture-leveling-desk` has a valid band, offer, promotion case, or comparable-work cohort unless that desk placed the role against the level guide rather than against the title someone wanted; every compa-ratio and every pay equity grouping inherits that placement. Nothing `candidate-evaluation-debrief-desk` produces is defensible unless `structured-interview-design-desk` fixed the rubric before anyone was assessed against it, which is why loop design sits ahead of the loop rather than inside it. And `people-analytics-desk` is only ever as good as the codes entered upstream: the disposition code at rejection, the job code on the record, the regretted flag, and the separation reason at exit are all set in the stages that create them, and no reporting stage can reconstruct them later.

Each entry states the hard halt specific to that stage. The default posture everywhere else is to proceed with the assumption labeled inline against the requisition, role, candidate, employee, cohort, cycle, case, or metric it affects, per `references/halt-taxonomy.md`.

## Contracts

### workforce-planning-desk
Requires: the current headcount reconciled to the system of record on a stated date with contractors, interns, and accepted-but-not-started hires counted or excluded explicitly, the approved plan and its fiscal calendar, budget by org unit with whether it is fully loaded or base only, attrition history with its definitions, the org shape as spans and layers rather than as a chart, the work the plan is meant to deliver, location and entity constraints, and the approval authority for headcount and for any reduction.
Owns: the headcount plan by org unit, level, and location against the work it funds, the build against develop against contract decision for each gap with the assumption behind it, the attrition assumption stated with the window it came from, the requisition set with each opening classified as incremental, backfill, replacement, conversion, or reorganization, the backfill comparison naming the vacated position's level and pay where that is what the argument turns on, the capacity gaps the plan does not close stated rather than absorbed, the requisition approval state with the named approver and the fiscal period the cost lands in, and the scenario variants where more than one plan is live.
Hands to: `job-architecture-leveling-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. Headcount, budget, an org change, or a reduction would be adopted or a requisition opened. Each commits money the organization has to find and, in a reduction, the jobs of named people; a plan circulating as though it were approved starts hiring conversations, reorganization rumors, and retention risk that no later correction reverses.

### job-architecture-leveling-desk
Requires: the job architecture and level guide in force with its version, the family and sub-family structure, the band set with effective dates and geographic differentials, existing incumbents in the family and their placements, the actual work of the role in terms of scope, autonomy, and impact, the exemption or classification tests that apply in the jurisdiction of employment, the posting obligations for each location the role can be filled in, and the equivalent roles the market prices.
Owns: the level placement argued in the language of the level guide rather than in the language of the title requested, the job family, sub-family, and job code, the grade and band mapping with the band version behind it, the exemption or classification determination with the test applied and the jurisdiction it was applied under, the job description separating what the work requires from what a previous incumbent happened to have, must-have criteria each tied to something the work actually needs, success measures written so they can be assessed at six and twelve months, the posted range and any other jurisdictional posting content, and the leveling comparators so the placement can be defended against the team it sits in.
Hands to: `sourcing-pipeline-desk`.
Hard halt: release integrity. A level placement or an exemption classification would be asserted without the level guide or the test behind it. Classification is a wage and hour position that applies to everyone sharing the job code, not to one person; getting it wrong creates back pay, penalties, and in some jurisdictions a collective claim, and the level placement it sits on becomes the anchor for every band, offer, promotion case, and comparable-work cohort downstream.

### sourcing-pipeline-desk
Requires: the approved requisition and the job definition with its posted range, the channels available with their historical volume, pass-through, and cost, the talent market for the level and location, referral and agency terms including fees, guarantees, and eligibility, the applicant tracking configuration and its disposition code set, the record-keeping obligations for applicant data in each jurisdiction, current funnel state with time in stage, and the candidate experience commitments the team has made.
Owns: the sourcing plan with the channel mix and what each is expected to produce, the funnel with counts, pass-through rates carrying their denominators, and time in stage by step, the pipeline coverage judgment stating plainly where a pipeline is one candidate wearing a process, the diagnosis of where the funnel actually loses people separated from where it is merely slow, the disposition code discipline so a rejection reason is recorded as the reason rather than as a shrug, the candidate experience gaps with the step that causes each, the agency and referral position with its commercial terms, and the applicant record retention position for each jurisdiction in scope.
Hands to: `structured-interview-design-desk`.
Hard halt: production or destructive. A posting would go live, outreach would be sent, or candidates would be contacted or dispositioned in the applicant tracking system. A live posting is a public document carrying a legally required pay range in several jurisdictions, outreach at volume reaches people who did not ask and is attributed to the company permanently, and a disposition written into the system is the record an audit reads years later.

### structured-interview-design-desk
Requires: the level guide and the competencies the role actually needs at that level, the interviewer pool with who is calibrated and who is not, the time the loop can reasonably occupy on both sides, existing rubrics and question banks with their known weaknesses, any assessment or work sample under consideration with whatever validity evidence exists for it, the lawful question boundaries and data collection timing rules in each jurisdiction the role can be filled in, and the process adjustment path for candidates who request one.
Owns: the loop design with each stage assigned a competency so coverage is deliberate rather than incidental, the rubric with level anchors that describe observable behavior instead of adjectives, the question set mapped to competencies with follow-up probes that get to evidence, the work sample scoped to what the job requires with its time cost to the candidate and whether it is paid, the interviewer assignment and calibration position including reviewer variance where it is known, the instruction that scorecards are recorded before the debrief, the question boundaries stated per jurisdiction, and the accommodation path recorded as a process adjustment without the underlying condition entering the hiring record.
Hands to: `candidate-evaluation-debrief-desk`.
Hard halt: security or privacy. The loop or an assessment would collect information the jurisdiction prohibits or restricts by timing, including salary history, criminal record before the permitted stage, health or disability information, immigration status beyond eligibility to work, family or caregiving status, or anything from which a protected characteristic is being inferred. The information cannot be unlearned once it is in the file, its presence taints every decision that follows, and the candidate is the party who carries the consequence.

### candidate-evaluation-debrief-desk
Requires: the fixed rubric and the loop as designed, every scorecard with its evidence and the date it was written, the completeness of the loop including interviews that did not happen, the level the candidate was assessed against, reference and background check state with what each is permitted to cover, internal candidate status where it applies, competing candidates in the same pipeline, the disposition code set, and the decision authority for a hire at this level.
Owns: the debrief synthesis built from evidence rather than from impression, with each claim traced to the interviewer and the observation behind it, the recommendation stated as hire, no hire, hire at a different level, or insufficient evidence, dissent preserved rather than averaged into a consensus that nobody held, the gaps the loop did not test named as gaps instead of filled by inference, the level check where the evidence supports a different placement than the one the loop assumed, the rejection reason recorded so it matches the scorecards, the internal candidate outcome with the follow-up that keeps a rejected internal from becoming a resignation, and the pass-through read by stage where the population supports it.
Hands to: `offer-compensation-desk`.
Hard halt: release integrity. A hire or no hire recommendation, or the disposition recorded against it, would rest on an incomplete loop, on scorecards written after the debrief, or on impression presented as evidence. The disposition code and the scorecards are the entire defensible record of why this person was chosen and that one was not, they are what an adverse impact challenge is answered with, and a recommendation assembled from what the room felt is indistinguishable from a real one until it has to be produced.

### offer-compensation-desk
Requires: the hiring recommendation with its evidence, the level placement and the band with its version and geographic differential, current pay for the existing team at that level, market data with its survey, cut, effective date, and aging, the budget approved on the requisition, the equity pool position and instrument terms, the approval chain with authority levels, the contingencies that apply including background check, right to work, references, and immigration, the candidate's stated expectation and constraints, and the rules on what may lawfully be asked and disclosed in this jurisdiction.
Owns: the offer model with base, variable, equity, sign-on, and relocation each stated with its mechanism and its conditions, the band position as range penetration or compa-ratio against a named band version, the internal comparator read that surfaces compression before it is created rather than after the team discovers it, the total cost against the approved budget, the approval chain with each approver, authority level, and state, the contingencies separated into those that must clear before a start date and those that need not, the offer expiry and start date with what each depends on, the close plan and the counteroffer position, and the decline reason captured as the candidate gave it.
Hands to: `onboarding-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. An offer would be extended, or pay, equity, a start date, or a contingency waiver committed. An extended offer is a commitment a candidate resigns their job against; rescinding one is the most damaging single act in this suite, and every number in it is anchored the moment it is spoken, including for the next person hired into the same team.

### onboarding-desk
Requires: the accepted offer with its start date and any contingency still open, the role definition with its success measures, the manager and their availability in the first weeks, the provisioning, equipment, and access requirements with their lead times, the employment eligibility verification rules and the statutory window they run in, the benefits enrollment windows and their deadlines, the required policy acknowledgments, the training obligations for the role and jurisdiction, and the ramp expectation the team actually holds.
Owns: the pre-start plan with owners and lead times so day one is not spent waiting for a laptop, the eligibility verification position stating the window and its state without specifying which documents a person must produce, the day one and first week sequence, the thirty, sixty, and ninety day milestones written as observable outcomes rather than as topics, the manager's commitments with dates against them, the buddy or mentor assignment, the acknowledgment and training completion position, the benefits and payroll enrollment deadlines that are the person's to miss, and the early attrition signals that have actually been observed.
Hands to: `people-operations-records-desk`.
Hard halt: security or privacy. Onboarding is where the largest volume of a person's sensitive data arrives at once: government identifiers, bank details, eligibility documents, dependants, and benefits elections. Halt where the plan would over-collect, retain copies the rules do not permit, route this data through a channel not approved for it, specify which documents a person must present rather than accepting what the rules allow, or place any of it in a file a manager can read. Data collected on day one sits in the record for the person's whole tenure and beyond it.

### people-operations-records-desk
Requires: the system of record and its effective dating model, the payroll and equity administration records, the executed offer letter or employment agreement, the org hierarchy and cost centre structure, the transaction being recorded with its effective date and the approval behind it, the downstream systems the record feeds, the retention schedule and access model for personnel documents, and the reconciliation state between systems as of a stated date.
Owns: the transaction specification with the field, the prior value, the new value, the effective date, and the approval that authorizes it, the effective dating position so a retroactive change is recognized as a payroll event rather than an edit, the org hierarchy integrity including managers of record who have left and positions reporting to nobody, the data quality findings that make downstream reporting wrong such as unmapped job codes, missing location, and stale employment basis, the reconciliation between the system of record, payroll, and equity administration with the differences named rather than averaged, the document retention and access position, and the record set that later stages will trust without re-reading.
Hands to: `performance-review-calibration-desk`.
Hard halt: source conflict. The system of record, payroll, equity administration, and the executed offer letter disagree on pay, level, manager, entity, hours, or a date. Preserve every reading with its as-of date, because the contract is what an employee can enforce, payroll is what actually reached their bank, and the system of record is what every report, band, and equity calculation in this suite is built from. Adopting the convenient reading silently converts a pay error into a reporting fact.

### performance-review-calibration-desk
Requires: the cycle definition with its period and the rating scheme's stated meaning at each point, the population in scope with the exclusion rule for tenure, leave, and recent hires, the goals or expectations the period was actually run against, self assessments and peer or upward input with their attribution state, the evidence managers can produce for each proposed rating, distribution guidance stated as guidance or as a constraint, prior cycle ratings, calibration group membership, and the approval and communication path.
Owns: the rating proposals with the evidence behind each and an explicit split between ratings resting on observed work and ratings resting on impression, the write-up quality position naming conclusions that carry no example, the calibration inputs prepared so the session compares like with like, the calibration record with every movement, its direction, and the reason recorded at the time it moved, the distribution before and after with the guidance identified for what it is, the consistency read across managers and any pattern by tenure, level, location, or population where the counts support it, the unresolved ratings kept open rather than defaulted, and the communication package with what each employee is told and by whom.
Hands to: `career-framework-progression-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. A rating would be communicated, or a performance outcome delivered, before calibration and approval are complete. A rating spoken to an employee cannot be revised downward without doing more damage than the original error, it becomes the basis on which that person decides whether to stay, and it is the document quoted back in every promotion, compensation, and separation decision that follows.

### career-framework-progression-desk
Requires: the level guide with the criteria for the target level and its version, the employee's demonstrated work at that level with dates, the calibrated rating and its evidence, the peer set already at the target level, tenure in level and any time-based expectation the framework sets, the promotion budget and its approval path, the dual track structure where management and individual contribution diverge, internal mobility postings and eligibility rules, and the denial and deferral practice the framework actually follows.
Owns: the promotion case argued from work already performed at the next level rather than from potential or from tenure, mapped criterion by criterion with the unmet ones named, the calibration of the case against the peer set already at that level, the compensation impact with the resulting band position and its approval state, the effective date and what it means for the next cycle, the denial or deferral written so it can be said to the person and survive being said, the specific gap and the work that would close it with a date, the dual track guidance where a strong individual contributor is being pushed into management by default, and the internal mobility position including who is blocked and by whom.
Hands to: `talent-review-succession-desk`.
Hard halt: release integrity. A promotion or a denial would be recorded against criteria the level guide does not contain, or a case would be argued from potential, tenure, or retention pressure rather than from work already performed at the next level. These decisions are compared across a cohort by the people in it within a week, the denial reason is the one thing the employee remembers verbatim, and a promotion granted on an unwritten standard is the precedent every subsequent case is argued against.

### talent-review-succession-desk
Requires: the roles that are actually critical and what they are critical to, incumbents with tenure, level, and calibrated performance, the internal candidates who could hold each role and what is missing, the development actions already committed and their state, retention signal for the people the plan depends on, the confidentiality tier the review runs at and who is in the room, the mobility constraints including location, entity, and visa, and the assessment criteria in use with their known subjectivity.
Owns: the critical role list justified by consequence rather than by seniority, the succession bench per role with ready now, ready later, and no successor stated plainly instead of softened, key person risk named with what actually happens next week if that person resigns, development plans with the named gap, the action, the owner, and the date, the potential assessment with the criteria applied and their subjectivity acknowledged, the internal mobility moves in flight or blocked with the blocker named, and the handling rules for a document that discusses people who have not been told any of this.
Hands to: `manager-enablement-desk`.
Hard halt: security or privacy. Talent review content would reach someone outside the review, be recorded in a system managers can browse, or be implied to an employee. Successor lists, potential placements, flight risk assessments, and "not ready" judgments are written about people who have not been told and in most cases must not be; a leaked grid ends the career conversation it was meant to enable, damages the person it names, and ends the program's usefulness permanently.

### manager-enablement-desk
Requires: the manager population in scope including new managers and managers of managers, the capability evidence that actually exists such as review write-up quality, survey scores on the team, attrition and its regretted share, and case volume, the cycle in flight and what managers must do in it and by when, the expectations set for one-to-ones, feedback, and check-ins, the escalation paths into the owning functions, the support already available, and the situation the manager is actually holding right now.
Owns: the capability position with the evidence behind each gap rather than a list of desirable manager traits, the cycle support built for the moment the manager needs it instead of the month before, the guidance for the specific conversation being prepared with the words that carry the message and the ones that create a commitment nobody approved, the manager's own boundary made explicit so a matter that belongs to employee relations, leave, or legal is routed the moment it is described, the new manager transition with the team inherited and what that team was told, the escalation path with what each function needs at handoff, and the practice standards that are enforceable rather than aspirational.
Hands to: `engagement-retention-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. A manager would be equipped to deliver a rating, a compensation outcome, a discipline step, a promotion denial, or a separation message ahead of the approval the owning desk requires, or would be coached to handle themselves a matter that became the company's notice the moment they described it: a harassment or discrimination report, a protected leave request, an accommodation request, a safety concern, or a whistleblowing disclosure. The company is on notice from the manager's knowledge, not from the case file, and the gap between those two dates is the exposure.

### engagement-retention-desk
Requires: the survey instrument and version with whether items are comparable to prior runs, the invited population and the response counts by cut, the confidentiality threshold and suppression rules, the results with their comparison periods and any population change between them, verbatim comments, attrition data with voluntary, involuntary, regretted, and unregretted separated and defined, exit and stay interview content, manager and team structure for the cuts being reported, and the action commitments made after the last run and what happened to them.
Owns: the results read at the cuts the response rates can actually support, with groups where the rate makes the result unreadable named rather than reported, the confidentiality position including the minimum group size and complementary suppression so a small cell cannot be recovered by subtraction from its siblings and the total, verbatim themes written so no comment identifies its author, the driver analysis stating what the data supports as associated with the outcome and what is leadership's prior belief, the retention risk by role and population with the signal behind each, regretted attrition with who decides regretted and on what basis, the action plans with an owner, a commitment, and a date, and the honest account of last cycle's commitments, because an unanswered survey is worse than no survey.
Hands to: `compensation-review-cycle-desk`.
Hard halt: security or privacy. A result would be reported below the confidentiality threshold, published in a cut from which an individual response can be recovered, or a verbatim reproduced in a form that identifies its author. Employees answer on a confidentiality promise, one identified comment ends honest responses across the company for years, and the manager who reads a four-person team score already knows who said what.

### compensation-review-cycle-desk
Requires: the budget pool with what it is a percentage of, the band set in force with effective dates and geographic differentials, market survey data with the survey, cut, effective date, and aging applied, current pay for the population with basis and effective dates, calibrated performance ratings, promotion increases funded separately, the merit model and how performance, band position, and tenure enter it, pay transparency and reporting obligations per jurisdiction, and the approval path for the pool and for individual exceptions.
Owns: the band refresh with what moved, by how much, and who is now below range as a result, the merit model with its mechanics stated rather than implied, the proposed changes with each employee's increase, resulting band position, and rationale, promotion increases held separately from merit because they are a different decision funded differently, the compression and inversion read naming the people whose pay has been overtaken by new hires or by their own reports, the pay equity analysis with its cohort basis, method, controls, and the gap the controls do not explain, remediation proposed with its cost and approval state, the transparency obligations per jurisdiction with what must be disclosed and to whom, and the total against the approved pool.
Hands to: `policy-handbook-desk`.
Hard halt: release integrity. A market position, a band, or a pay equity finding would be asserted without the survey cut, effective date, and aging behind it, or without the cohort basis, controls, and what those controls legitimately explain. These figures leave the company: in several jurisdictions a pay gap or a range disclosure is a regulated filing, and a "we pay at market" claim made to a population becomes a promise. A finding of no gap produced by controlling for the variable that carries the bias is worse than no analysis, because it is now on the record as a review.

### policy-handbook-desk
Requires: the policy set in force with versions and effective dates, the jurisdictions the policy covers and the statutory floors in each, the executed agreements and any collective or works council agreement the policy interacts with, the practice as it is actually followed where it has diverged from the written rule, the consultation and notice obligations a change triggers, the acknowledgment mechanism and its records, the exceptions already granted and the precedent each set, and the change that is being requested and what it is meant to fix.
Owns: the policy draft written so a manager can apply it without calling someone, the jurisdictional matrix stating where the global text holds and where a local addendum is required, the change summary including what it changes for people who relied on the prior version and whether the change can lawfully apply retroactively, the consultation position with the trigger and who must be engaged before anything is published, the acknowledgment model with who must acknowledge and by when, the exception register with the approver and the precedent each creates, the conflicts between the draft, existing policy, executed contracts, and local floors, and the practice divergence surfaced as a finding, because an unenforced policy is worse than no policy in a dispute.
Hands to: `employee-relations-desk`.
Hard halt: source conflict. A provision conflicts with a statutory floor, an executed employment agreement, or a collective agreement, or two jurisdictions the same policy covers require opposite things. Preserve both readings, because publishing a single global text over that conflict either breaches the floor in one place or grants an unintended entitlement everywhere else, and a handbook provision that contradicts a contract is read against the company by default in most forums.

### employee-relations-desk
Requires: the report as the reporting party made it and in their words, the parties and their reporting relationships, whether protected activity is present because it sets the retaliation window and the review path, the policy in force at the version effective on the date of the events, the documented history for any performance or conduct matter, the evidence available including records, messages, and system logs with what may lawfully be accessed, the interim measures available, the standard of proof the organization applies, the confidentiality and privilege position, and the approval and legal review path for any outcome.
Owns: the intake record with the allegation as reported and the date the company was on notice, the protected activity determination with the retaliation window it opens, interim measures chosen so they do not disadvantage the reporting party, the investigation plan with scope, interviews, documents, and what is deliberately out of scope, the interview record separating what each person said from what was corroborated by something other than an account, findings stated per allegation as substantiated, unsubstantiated, or inconclusive rather than as one verdict for the case, the outcome recommendation with the comparable prior outcomes it is consistent with, the retaliation monitoring window with an owner and what is being watched, and the closure communication written differently for each party because each is entitled to different information.
Hands to: `leave-accommodation-desk`.
Hard halt: approval. Discipline, a suspension, a demotion, a final warning, a performance improvement plan, or a termination would be issued, or a finding communicated, before the investigation is complete and the required approvals and employment law review are in place. Adverse action ahead of findings makes the investigation a formality, and the file records the sequence in dates that cannot be rearranged later; where protected activity is present the same action is read as retaliation regardless of its merits.

### leave-accommodation-desk
Requires: the request as made and the jurisdiction of employment, the statutory and company leave categories available and their interaction where they stack or run concurrently, the entitlement calculation with the look-back or accrual method, the job protection window, the pay treatment components and their sources, the accommodation request stated as a limitation on the work, the essential functions of the role as actually documented, the medical information handling and storage rules, the return to work and review process, and the payroll, benefits, and manager coordination path.
Owns: the entitlement determination with the categories that apply, how they interact, and how the amount was computed, the dates with expected return and the job protection window's end, the pay treatment with the source of each component, the interactive process record with each exchange, its date, what was proposed, and by whom, the accommodation assessment against the essential functions with alternatives considered and the reason each was accepted or not, the medical information held apart from the personnel file with access named, the manager communication carrying the restriction and the dates without the condition behind them, the return to work plan with any restriction and its review date, and the coverage plan for the work while the person is away.
Hands to: `offboarding-separation-desk`.
Hard halt: security or privacy. Medical information, a diagnosis, or the reason for a leave would reach a manager, a team, a shared system, or the personnel file. The manager is entitled to the restriction and the dates and nothing else; a diagnosis in a personnel file follows the person through every later decision and colours it, and in most jurisdictions the disclosure is a separate violation from whatever prompted it. Denying or delaying an accommodation or a protected leave is an adverse action in its own right and belongs behind the approval and legal review path, never inside a workflow run.

### offboarding-separation-desk
Requires: the separation type and the documented basis distinguished from the account being given now, the notice required by contract, statute, and any collective agreement, the last day and whether it is a working day or a payroll date, the final pay components and the jurisdiction's timing rule for delivering them, accrued time and benefits treatment, severance and release terms with their consideration and revocation periods, the approvals required including employment law review, the reduction in force selection criteria and pool where one applies, access and asset inventory, and what only this person knows.
Owns: the separation packet with the basis, the notice position, and the terms, final pay computed against the jurisdiction's timing rule before the date is set, the release position with its consideration and revocation periods where one is offered, the approval chain including employment law review where protected activity, a leave, an accommodation, a complaint, or a consultation obligation is present, the reduction in force selection criteria fixed and documented before names with the resulting slate tested for adverse impact, the access revocation schedule tied to the conversation rather than preceding it, knowledge transfer for what only this person holds with the named receiver, the exit interview with what was said kept distinct from what was concluded, and the coded separation reason and rehire eligibility that every attrition figure downstream inherits.
Hands to: `people-analytics-desk`.
Hard halt: production or destructive. A separation would be executed, notice given, access revoked, final pay released, or a reduction in force slate notified. Every one of these is final on the day it happens: access revoked before the conversation tells the person before their manager does, final pay released late triggers per-day penalties in several jurisdictions, and a termination stands whatever the file says afterward. The sequence exists because the steps are irreversible in the order they occur.

### people-analytics-desk
Requires: the metric definitions actually in force with their exact computation, the source systems behind each and any difference between the raw record and the reporting layer, the population with its exclusions and the denominator convention, the codes entered upstream including disposition, job, regretted, and separation reason with their known weaknesses, response counts and rates for anything survey derived, the reporting threshold and suppression rules, the comparison period and what changed in the population between them, the disclosure obligations for anything leaving the company, and the forum that will decide on the numbers.
Owns: each metric carrying its value, its written definition, its population, its exclusions, its denominator, its window, and its source, headcount reconciled to the system of record on a stated date with contractors, interns, employees on leave, and unstarted hires counted or excluded explicitly, attrition split into voluntary, involuntary, regretted, and unregretted each with its definition, time to fill and time to hire named as the different clocks they are, representation and pay gap reporting produced against the disclosure standard that applies with suppression applied across the whole cut set, the movement traced to the manager, level, band, or policy behind it rather than presented as a trend, the coding weaknesses that make a figure unusable stated rather than smoothed, and the decision each figure is being brought to the forum for.
Hands to: `people-talent-command-desk` for the program record, and back into the desks the forum directs work into.
Hard halt: release integrity. A figure would reach a board, a regulator, an auditor, a works council, or a public disclosure without its definition, population, denominator, and suppression, or a representation or pay gap number would be published in a form from which individuals can be identified. These numbers set headcount and budget, and in several jurisdictions they are a filing with legal consequences for being wrong. A reporting layer that exists and cannot be read is a connector halt; a figure nobody has ever computed is a soft gap and is reported as not measured.

## Packet rule

Every stage updates `people_packet` as defined in `references/suite-workflow-contract.md` before handing off. As-of dates, jurisdiction determinations, level placements, band versions, approval state, commitments already made to a person, statutory clocks, and the confidentiality tier of every artifact accumulate across stages and are never dropped to keep an artifact short. Anything removed from the record is removed with a reason and a date, because a promotion case, a pay equity cohort, an investigation, and a separation are all argued years later from the record as it stood at the time, and the question asked afterward is always what was known, what was documented, and on what date.
